resources.string: SyxDroid is a third-party launcher and needs your own files of Songs of Syx to work; it contains no part of the game. You must own a legal copy of the game. SyxDroid is not developed by, endorsed by or affiliated with Gamatron AB, the makers of Songs of Syx, and its developer takes no responsibility for any legal consequences of its use.
Shared by all instances. Safe to clear at any time: the renderer re-encodes what it needs, which costs a few seconds on the next load.

Compresses large textures with a minimal loss of quality for phone and even tablet screens. Comes with a cache you can clear yourself. The first launch builds the cache and may take a little longer. The cache is shared by ZINK and NG_GL4ES. Note: with ETC2 enabled the LIBGL_SHRINK variable becomes almost pointless, and no tile grid is drawn on textures.
Compresses large textures with minimal quality loss. Keeps a cache you can clear.
Renderer, driver, Java arguments, resolution and the on-screen controls belong to a game instance. Open them with the gear button on an instance card.
Long press on empty space to open context menu. Changes are saved automatically once you are finished
Full info shows a bar at the top: GPU and CPU load, memory, power draw, temperature and an FPS graph. Handy to see what slows the game down.

Lowers texture detail when memory runs low. Helps avoid crashes on devices with 8 GB RAM or less; not needed with 12 GB. Applies to the NG_GL4ES renderer on Build 42.

The first alpha of SyxDroid: Songs of Syx on Android, with your own copy of the game.

• Import the game from a zip of your Steam, Windows or Linux copy, or download it from Steam on the Game page.

• Several instances, the game's language, render resolution and a frame rate limit in the instance settings.

• On-screen controls with an editor: the Controls button in the bottom bar.

This is an alpha: expect rough edges. Report problems with Report a bug in the side menu.

Additional JVM arguments, e.g.:

• -Xmx2G - allocate 2Gb of memory
• -Xms512M - process starts with 512MB RAM
• -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=120 - target a shorter garbage-collector pause

In theory, it should help when there's not enough RAM. Some arguments are already set by settings.
If you set it incorrectly and the app doesn't run, reinstall it or just clear the app cache.

Values 1–11 are not a scale. Commonly used: 1 (ultra low) and 7 (balanced); mode 1 can crash on empty textures. See the table for the rest.

1. ⚠ all halved
2. ⚠ above 512px halved
3. ⚠ above 256px halved
4. ⚠ above 256px halved, 1024px+ quartered
5. above 256px → 256px
6. above 128px halved, 512px+ → 256px
7. above 512px halved

⚠ also shrinks empty textures — this is where the crashes come from.

8–11 are compatibility modes: they report a larger maximum texture size to the game and save no memory. Not needed for PZ.

Halving a side quarters the memory a texture costs.

Environment variables passed directly to the system before the game starts.

Use to configure renderers, drivers and other components, e.g.:

TU_DEBUG=nogmem
ZINK_DEBUG=norp

Use with caution — incorrect values may cause crashes.

On Build 41 this is the right choice: it runs on any GPU and needs no driver setup.\n\nOn Build 42 it does not work — you will get a black screen. There, use NG_GL4ES (any GPU) or ZINK (Adreno).

Recommended for Build 42: caps the Java heap and returns memory to the system, which leaves room for the renderer. In some cases the game may fail to start without some of these parameters. Not for Build 41 — on 4 GB devices it does more harm than good.

This renderer was written for Build 42 and does not work on Build 41 — the game will not start. On Build 41 choose GL4ES.\n\nBuild 42 also wants its own Java arguments — the suggested preset sets everything at once: Settings → Suggested presets.
